This isn't really what I expected it to be, tbh. When I heard "Shelter but online" I was excited! Surviving in a vast forest, hiding from or banding together with other players, just surviving? it sounded fun! But that's not what this game is at all. There's no surviving elements, no dangers, no food or water needs, you can't even die even if you fell from a thousand meter mountain, or completely through the map in one of the various void holes they decided would be a great addition (whyyyy are there random giant holes in the map in the first place? It doesn't really make sense or look good)... So is this more of a social or roleplaying game then? Not really... There is emotes, and your animal of choice can make sounds, but it's often not clear enough to get a point across, or to make other people understand you. There's not even a normal chat function. Not to mention how clunky the game feels to play. The movements are stiff and rigid. There's not much to do either, you can find obelisks that can open up, but it needs certain animals to be close to it, and you're usually playing in an empty server. There's collectibles, but I'm not even sure what they are for. Buying new animals? I play one for 15 minutes and another one gets unlocked, then I do the same thing on that one and I get a new one, and so on. So what are the points even for if not for the main thing this game offers?

I'm very disappointed. Feels like fans of the Shelter series would WANT an online survival game, but to instead get this... It feels a bit stale. I cannot recommend this to anyone, unless you like walking simulators.
An extremely visually striking game, that lets you run around and explore as a little critter, I cannot more strongly suggest this game if you like very laid-back exploration

I always appreciate multiplayer games that encourage teamwork and exploration, and creative social mechanics.

The concept of this game is really cute, and the art style and animal designs are absolutely beautiful! I really love how colorful and detailed everything is, and how big the world feels. Truly, if you have a passion for exploring colorful, unique, detailed landscapes, this is a game I'd point you toward!

Something to note about this game is that there are no chat systems. You cannot /talk/ to people you encounter. But there are a lot of helpful emotes and stickers you can use and unlock that let you get ideas across to your silent friends just fine :)

I only wish this game could be updated further, and had more players. It feels like it was abandoned when it still has so much potential to work with. I know the team behind this game lost a lot of staff not super long ago, and its hindered their development, but now that they've been working on other stuff, I hope they can come around to their past games and give them some TLC (because this game did use to get updated routinely until it stopped getting worked on outta nowhere).

But, nonetheless, it's a very relaxing and visually pleasing experience. If you're a fan of the other shelter games, and you want a more calm, social, laid back experience, then you'll likely love this one! 💙

Meadow, el último título de la saga Shelter, es un juego que destaca por su atmósfera relajante y su mundo vivo, ideal para quienes buscan una experiencia tranquila y contemplativa. Desde el primer momento, la combinación de exploración, interacción con otros jugadores y la estética natural del juego transmite una sensación de calma que pocas veces se ve en otros MMO de tipo “animal”. El sistema de charlas dentro del juego es particularmente notable: permite conectar con otros jugadores de manera orgánica, sin presión, y fomenta una comunidad que realmente se siente parte del ecosistema del juego.

Sin embargo, no todo es perfecto. Uno de los puntos que menos me ha gustado es la dependencia de compras anteriores para desbloquear ciertos personajes. Para poder acceder a algunos de ellos, necesitas haber adquirido otros títulos de la saga Shelter o incluso la saga completa de la productora, lo cual puede ser frustrante para los jugadores nuevos que no quieran invertir tanto dinero solo para disfrutar de todo el contenido.

Otro inconveniente es el ritmo de vida del juego. Durante el día, el mundo se siente prácticamente “muerto”, con muy poca actividad en los servidores. Curiosamente, es a partir de las 12 de la noche, hora española, cuando los servidores muestran algo de vida y movimiento. Esto puede complicar la experiencia para quienes solo pueden jugar en horarios más convencionales.

Además, aunque el juego brilla por su relajación y exploración, quizá se echa en falta algún tipo de sistema de interacción más competitivo, como combates o un componente PvP a nivel housing o territorial. Algo así podría añadir una capa de dinamismo para los jugadores que buscan un desafío adicional, sin comprometer la esencia tranquila de Meadow.

A pesar de estos inconvenientes, Meadow sigue siendo un juego altamente recomendable. Su mundo está cuidado al detalle, la sensación de comunidad es agradable y el diseño general es excepcional. Si lo que buscas es una experiencia relajante, con exploración y conexión social en un universo bonito y bien pensado, Meadow cumple con creces.

Recomendado para quienes disfruten de la calma y la interacción ligera, pero con ciertas reservas para quienes busquen contenido más activo o competitivo.

Начну с того, что попала ко мне эта игра еще в свое золотое время, когда на серверах было много людей. Все собирались в огромные группы животных и ходили по серверу фармя фрагменты открывающие скины или новых животных. Но со временем игра сама себя и загнала в тупик, так как все бесплатные животные уже были открыты, а что бы получить новых нужно было скупать все игры Shelter, что выходило не дешево ради одного животного покупать целую игру. Так и осталась игра в простое, новых бесплатных животных не добавляли, а платных никто не хотел покупать. Зайдя в игру в 2026 году, увидела от силы только 6 человек на сервере, подключившись, буквально через 3 минуты меня выкинуло на рабочий стол. Зайдя снова в игру уже писалось, что сервера недоступны. Увы игра не подается как отдельных продукт от франшизы Shelter, а просто как бесплатное дополнение с коопом.  На сегодняшних день, могу с уверенностью заявить, что золотые временя этой игры остались в далеком прошлом, разработчики сами постепенно убивали эту игру, дабы срубить по больше денег с продукции Shelter, сервера уже доживают последние свои дни, смысла в нее играть уже нет. А ведь могла получится действительно неплохой симулятор животных со своей изюминкой в плане графики, мне она даже зашла, я играла в первый и второй Shelter и графика добавляла душевности в эти игры, и я бы была не против поиграть и в симулятор с онлайном, бегая с другими игроками. Оглядываясь назад могу сказать, что воспоминания об этой игре остались у меня только приятные, но сегодня я прощаюсь с этой игрой.

趁着80%off的春促写个评测！
很随性且放松的游戏，不知为什么总让我想起星际拓荒——但比那还漫无目的。Meadow可以说就是一个动物扮演前提下的步行模拟器。

玩家对于探索和收集的欲望是meadow最大的游玩动力：游戏里没有任务，没有升级，没有战斗，没有死亡。唯一勉强称得上“主线”的只有一件事：收集各类植物、碎片、方尖碑，以解锁新的动物以及皮肤。
当然，你可以给自己安排任务：比如探索不同可游玩动物之间的差别（移速、跳跃高度、叫声、动作差异）；沉浸式对动物进行扮演，在地图上寻找巢穴、饮用溪水、享用食物，用有限的动作与表情与其他动物玩家以符合食物链的方式互动；试图摸清楚整个地图，包括地上和地下的路径；每月都去寻找位置不同、造型不同的本月专属动物雕像；收集全动物，全皮肤，或者全部的Steam成就……
总之，要做什么完全由你决定。什么都不做也可以。

而我同样相当喜欢的一个设计是，游戏里，与其他玩家之间的互动只能用简单的符号和动物叫声表达。没有文字交流，当然更没有属于人类的语音交流，一切都很原始和符号化。我真的十分享受在这个基础上与陌生玩家的相识和互动。游戏甚至自带匿名功能（可自由选择是否开启），其他玩家看不见你的名称、你也看不见其他人的——也因此很适合体验各种随机且随性的相识、相遇、相伴和分离。
在一切匿名的前提下，一次分离就是永别，因为我永远没法知道下次再和它相遇会是什么时候；又或者，即便下次遇见相同的动物，我也无法预测背后会是怎样的玩家。但从另一个角度来说，哪怕换了不同的动物、皮肤、叫声，一些熟悉的表情习惯、行为甚至是卡顿频率（。）都能让我不由自主微笑起来，会有种似是而非的、遇上了曾经短暂相伴的动物伙伴的朦胧的快乐。
不过话又说话来……我这么玩是因为我真的很享受一期一会的体验，且非常不热衷于在游戏外建立任何基于游戏的社交关系。如果其他玩家更喜欢有固定的游戏搭子、希望能通过meadow认识更多的朋友，虽然现在还活跃的玩家不多，但在Steam论坛/Discord上还是有不少活人的。或者说只要选择不开启匿名功能，一场游戏下来说不定就能收获好几个新朋友了呢（非匿名的前提下，游戏里有按键能显示在场玩家的Steam用户名）。

总之，可以想象，它不是适合所有人的游戏 。加上现在距离发售已经快10年了，服务器基本都成了鬼服……不过就我一个月来的游玩体验来看，至少欧服还有不少人玩，最多的时候能有10+个玩家同时在线。和刚发售时的旺期肯定不能比，但这个人数对我来说其实相当正好。尤其是欧洲时间的晚上，经常能和1-5个动物玩家一起组成动物探索队，一起快乐地收集地图里的资源。因为每个玩家的游玩习惯和对meadow的熟悉程度都十分不同，每次合作游玩都能收获些新的体验，这一点真的十分难得。

一言以蔽之，meadow很适合
[list]
    [*]喜欢且享受在游戏世界里漫无目的地行走，
    [*]喜欢探索、收集、看风景，且能在无任务、无需求、无社交的前提下自娱自乐，
    [*]喜欢扮演动物，
    [*]不想和其他玩家以正常方式进行交流/好奇无文字的前提下如何交流
[/list]
……的玩家。

总之，趁着好价买来玩玩试试吧（怂恿）！

I genuinely miss this game. Nowadays it's very much dead, with little to no players. Every once in a while you'll see three or slightly more online. 

Before Might and Delight left it alone, and the player population went down significantly, it was a wonderful and fun experience. There's no chat, you can only communicate through emotes, and honestly that made the gameplay a lot more enjoyable and peaceful. With two or more players you could interact with the obelisks to break them and get shards, which depending on their colors, would help you unlock another animal, and more skins and emotes (some animals and skins you need to unlock by buying other Shelter games, and Meadow story books, however). You can find those shards throughout the map without needing an extra player to open the obelisks, but it's a lot more grinding, and it's a bit hard to find anyone else in the game today to help you out.

Today, I felt incredibly bored, I wanted to play a game so I could desperately get out of the boredom. Scrolled through my steam library and found Meadow there. I remembered how dead it is, but a wave of nostalgia overtook me and motivated me to install it and boot it up, and to my surprise there was 4 people online! Hopped on my Lynx and just roamed about, and found a little Lynx cub, another player! We exchanged waving emotes and roamed the map together, opening any obelisks we found that only needed two players. Then we came across a Fox, they decided to follow us too, but they suddenly crashed and we had to leave em behind after waiting a few minutes to see if they'd come back :( Eventually I had to hop off for the night, it was getting late, but in the end, it was a great time, and reminded me of the older days when Meadow was a lot more active...

I don't have much hope that Might and Delight will try to make this game active again, they had done so before, but it didn't seem to work out. They're also focused on other games they're developing, which I understand honestly. But still, I thank them so much, for making such a wonderful game that has given me some good memories.

Meadow is, ultimately, the most distinctive game within the Shelter saga; despite being part of the series, it is not and does not seek to be like the other games. Instead of forcing you to survive by instinct or to take care of your offspring, as in the previous titles, Meadow encourages contemplation of its identity, which is what most characterizes all the games in the saga!!

Here, you don’t need to hunt or survive; it’s just you, a world to explore, and players (who are currently almost nonexistent) to spend time with. Because regardless of the animal you are—whether a badger, a frog, a fox, or a lynx—you are not forced to be something specific or to act in a certain way; you are the one who directs your own role. And although the game doesn’t explain this at first glance, roleplay is fundamental to understanding the reason behind Meadow’s existence.
There is something very important that must be clarified: the game currently has no players, and if there are any, they are very few...

Despite being a game designed to function as a massive multiplayer experience (though obviously not in the traditional sense), its player base is no longer what it once was, and it never aimed to have the largest number of players either. Generally, you will be alone as soon as you enter the game, and although you may occasionally run into a single player on any server, it is extremely unlikely

Therefore, if for some specific reason you are looking to play this game precisely for its online dynamic, you will probably need to look for other options

That said, it is important to clarify that the game is not defined, and never was defined, by how many players it has, but by those who continue to appreciate what it was and still is—both for what this game represents and what the rest of the saga represents as well. Evidently, it is not a saga that stands out for its complexity, because it was not developed with that goal in mind; it leans much more toward contemplation of its atmosphere and appreciation of nature, and in this game, that is fully realized

Ultimately, Meadow exists as an independent space, with gameplay more focused on the experience itself, and as such, it asks nothing more of you than to relax and appreciate its world...

It is a beautiful game, just as the entire Shelter saga is <3

This game provides a perfectly patient little space where every silent stranger is an opportunity for communal adventure and exploration. Entering as a badger cub, there's the briefest of 'tutorials' before it sends you off into the world, leaving you in the hands of your peers and quickly establishing the goal that is... Collecting flowers, mushrooms, fruits, puzzle pieces, and exploring hidden caves, tall mountains, and steep cliffs alike. All, if you decide, while using a wide variety of emotes/actions to share the experiences with any other players you come across. Though it was released nearly 10 years ago now ((wow)), this game holds up extremely well and continues to singularly occupy a very specific niche with a surprisingly consistent group of people who've stuck around all this time. That alone speaks to the impact it's made in my opinion; So if the trailers and recounted stories from others interest you, please consider giving this meditative game a go.

Ich muss sagen, ich war zunächst zögerlich, als ich die Spielbeschreibung las: Ein "als Spiel getarntes Forum"? Nun gab es Meadow für ~2€ im Angebot, da kann man nicht falsch machen. Und ja, das "Spiel" ist überraschend gut. Und es ist zum Glück nicht wirklich ein "Forum".

Im Grunde handelt es sich um eine Art gemeinsame Schnitzeljagd mit Fokus auf Erkundung und Gemeinschaft. Meadow ist definitiv kein Speil für Einzelspieler, man wird da nicht weit kommen. Es gibt kein "Spielziel", auch kein "Game over". Für viele ist es aber das Ziel, Tier-Charaktere, Skins und Emotes zu sammeln - oder Steam Achievements. Oder aber einfach das Gefühl von Gemeinschaft zu erleben, wenn man sich als Gruppe auf eine Expedition in unbekannte Gefilde aufmacht.

Spieler, die Action, Kämpfe, Präzisions-Sprungkombinationen oder schwere Puzzles suchen, sind hier falsch.

Denn Meadow ist vom Design her darauf ausgelegt, kinderfreundlich zu sein. Das Spiel ist völlig gewaltfrei. Man ist anonym, wenn man nicht seinen Realnamen als Tiernamen verwendet. Es gibt nur eine begrenzte Auswahl an Emoticons, und sich mit denen zu beleidigen ist praktisch unmöglich. Und das ist gut so. Bei meinen Sessions bin ich stets auf Gruppen von Spielern gestoßen, die rücksichtsvoll waren, sich für Hilfe bedankt haben und die die Netiquette befolgt oder von anderen gelernt haben. Und genau das ist der Grund, warum ich Meadows uneingeschränkt für Kinder ab etwa 10 Jahren empfehlen kann.

Nicht alles ist jedoch perfekt:
Als Einsteiger wusste ich überhaupt nicht, was ich tun sollte und wie ich es tun sollte, hatte kryptische Hinweise auf "OUTDATED"-Missionen in der Bildschirmecke und dutzende Emotes, deren Bedeutung sich mir in manchen Fällen nicht erschloss. Zum großen Glück hat jemand einen "Beginner's Guide" geschrieben, den kann ich jedem ans Herz legen. Aber Grundlegendes hätte man im Spiel erklären müssen.

Außerdem stört es mich, dass hier zu offensichtlich mit Kaufanreizen für andere Spiele des Studios gearbeitet wird. "Kaufe Speil X von uns und du erhältst dieses neues Tier oder Skin." Bei einem Spiel für diese Zielgruppe finde ich sowas deplatziert.

Die Musik ist gut und unaufdringlich, die Grafik irgendwo zwischen Geschmackssache und gewöhnungsbedürftig. Dafür sind die Hardware-Anforderungen auch sehr niedrig.

Last but not least lebt das Spiel von seiner Community. An Wochenenden und nach Rabattaktionen kann man genügend Mitspieler finden, aber wenn man irgendwann nur allein oder zu zweit auf der riesigen Karte rumläuft, verfliegt der Reiz schnell.

Insgesamt bin ich wie gesagt positiv überrascht und seinen rabattierten Preis war mir Meadow mehr als Wert in Bezug auf den Spaß, den man dort mit anderen haben kann.

Meadow is a very particular kind of game. You will either be in the small camp of people who absolutely LOVE and adore it, or you may find yourself scratching your head and asking, "What is the point?"

The point is discovery. It's wonder. It's connection. You are a little critter exploring a breathing painting, finding other little critters (other players) and joining up to discover and unlock new things together. There is no chat, no mission logs, and no leveling up - communication occurs via symbols and gestures. It can be a relaxing, wholesome, and visually stunning experience if you approach it with an open mind.
Also, the soundtrack is one of the most chill things I've ever heard. Sometimes, I run this game just to have it on as background ambiance while I do other things.

There is no other game quite like Meadow, though if you're a fan of games such as WolfQuest and The Endless Forest, then this will surely be up your alley. I recommend this game to anyone who is either a fan of animal sims or looking for something different, stress-free, and artistically-driven.
